examples.title: Johnson City extension, L/s (SI)
examples.description: A main extension model with test calibration scenarios. The existing system is modelled as a reservoir and a pump based on a hydrant flow test, in Johnson City, Texas. A new loop of 300 mm and 200 mm main is tied into it. A fire hydrant junction passes 95 L/s with 14 m of residual pressure. Liters per second, with meters and millimeters.

examples.title: Johnson City extension, gpm (US)
examples.description: A main extension model with test calibration scenarios. The existing system is modelled as a reservoir and a pump based on a hydrant flow test, in Johnson City, Texas. A new loop of 12 inch and 8 inch main is tied into it. A fire hydrant junction passes 1,500 gpm with 20 psi of residual pressure. Gallons per minute, with feet and inches.

examples.title: Munday well and tank, L/s (SI)
examples.description: A well, pump, check valve, loop, and elevated tank, with a 24-hour extended period simulation and scenarios for Max day and Peak hour, in Munday, Texas. A fire hydrant junction passes 32 L/s with 14 m of residual pressure. Liters per second, with meters and millimeters.

examples.title: EPANET Net3, L/s (SI)
examples.description: An EPANET example at Novato, California, converted from gallons per minute, feet, and inches, with the world map behind it: 92 junctions, 3 tanks, and 2 reservoirs, no valves, about 8 km square. A 24-hour extended-period simulation, with a source trace from the Lake. Liters per second, with meters and millimeters.

examples.title: EPANET Net2, L/s (SI)
examples.description: An EPANET example at Branford, Connecticut, converted from gallons per minute, feet, and inches: 35 junctions and 1 tank, with no reservoir, no pump, and no valves, about 2 km by 4 km. Fluoride, a non-reactive substance, enters at one source. Liters per second, with meters and millimeters.

examples.title: Elm Street Center, gpm (US)
examples.description: Prescott Valley, Arizona: 17 junctions, 1 reservoir, and 1 pump. A commercial site solved for fire flow on top of maximum day demand, at one moment in time, drawn over a site plan. Gallons per minute, with feet and inches.

examples.title: Valve types, gpm (US)
examples.description: A hilltop reservoir feeds a hub through a PBV, with a PRV, PSV, FCV, TCV, and GPV branching off it, each one controlling at the solved state. Gallons per minute, with feet and inches.

examples.title: EPANET Net1, scenarios and controls, L/s (SI)
examples.description: Four scenarios under Base, the average day: Max day (demand multiplier 1.5) and Peak hour (2.25), each with a main break child. A fictional EPANET example with chlorine, 1 reservoir, 1 tank, 1 pump, and two rule-based controls. Liters per second, with meters and millimeters.
